title: Timeline and decision map
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Biographies: conviction, justice and legacy
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 70 (Timeline and decision map (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 70: Biography: Khalid ibn al-Walid (خالد بن الوليد), strategy and service. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

timeline.label: 625 CE
timeline.text: At Uhud, leads cavalry against the Muslims

timeline.label: 629 CE
timeline.text: At Mu'tah, takes command after three commanders are killed and brings the army home safely; the Prophet ﷺ calls him a sword of Allah

timeline.label: 634 CE
timeline.text: Marches an army across the Syrian desert

timeline.label: 642 CE
timeline.text: Dies in Homs, Syria, after continuing to serve under Abu Ubaydah

head: Decision
Quality
rows: accepting Islam after years of opposing it
serving loyally when Umar replaced him as overall commander

model.title: How does the biography present Khalid's change?

parts.text: Point: as a turning point that reveals humility
Evidence: he 'accepted Islam after years of opposing it'
Technique: contrast between his past and future
Zoom in: 'opposing' stresses how far he travelled
Analyse: changing course takes more courage than holding on

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The biography presents Khalid's change as humble courage: the contrast with years of 'opposing' Islam shows how far he had to travel to accept it.

keywords.def: a careful plan to achieve a goal
'Sword of Allah', the title the Prophet ﷺ gave Khalid
faithful support for a person or cause
self-control and keeping to what is right
the ability to make wise decisions

questions.q: What title did the Prophet ﷺ give him?
questions.a: Sayf Allah, a sword of Allah
he took command after three commanders were killed and brought the army home safely

questions.q: Core: complete the decision map: five decisions, the quality each shows and evidence
Extend: in the portal response box, write a PETZAAL paragraph: How does the writer present Khalid as a servant of his cause?
Stretch: compare how Ali and Khalid each showed conviction
What does Khalid's loyal service after being replaced as commander show?
options: he served the cause, not his own status
he was not a good leader
questions.a: A) he served the cause, not his own status. Accepting a lower position without complaint shows his service was for Allah and the community, not for status.
C) brought the army home safely

questions.q: One quality Khalid shows, with evidence
questions.a: For example: loyalty: he served under Abu Ubaydah without complaint
